14:32.en: Allah is He Who created the heavens and the earth, and causeth water to descend from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you, and maketh the ships to be of service unto you, that they may run upon the sea at His command, and hath made of service unto you the rivers

14:33.ar: وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ دَآئِبَيۡنِۖ وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ

33:12.ar: وَإِذۡ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ إِلَّا غُرُورࣰ ا
33:12.en: And when the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, were saying: Allah and His messenger promised us naught but delusion

33:22.ar: وَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ ٱلۡأَحۡزَابَ قَالُواْ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥۚ وَمَا زَادَهُمۡ إِلَّآ إِيمَٰنࣰ ا وَتَسۡلِيمࣰ ا

29:2.ar: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتۡرَكُوٓاْ أَن يَقُولُوٓاْ ءَامَنَّا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفۡتَنُونَ
29:2.en: Do men imagine that they will be left (at ease) because they say, We believe, and will not be tested with affliction

29:3.ar: وَلَقَدۡ فَتَنَّا ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۖ فَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْ وَلَيَعۡلَمَنَّ ٱلۡكَٰذِبِينَ
29:3.en: Lo! We tested those who were before you. Thus Allah knoweth those who are sincere, and knoweth those who feign

47:31.ar: وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ نَعۡلَمَ ٱلۡمُجَٰهِدِينَ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَنَبۡلُوَاْ أَخۡبَارَكُمۡ
47:31.en: And verily We shall try you till We know those of you who strive hard (for the cause of Allah) and the steadfast, and till We test your record

2:214.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتُمۡ أَن تَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأۡتِكُم مَّثَلُ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۖ مَّسَّتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءُ وَٱلضَّرَّآءُ وَزُلۡزِلُواْ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَ ٱلرَّسُولُ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ مَتَىٰ نَصۡرُ ٱللَّهِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ نَصۡرَ ٱللَّهِ قَرِيبࣱ‏
2:214.en: Or think ye that ye will enter paradise while yet there hath not come unto you the like of (that which came to) those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them, they were shaken as with earthquake, till the messenger (of Allah) and those who believed along with him said: When cometh Allah's help? Now surely Allah's help is nigh

10:98.ar: فَلَوۡلَا كَانَتۡ قَرۡيَةٌ ءَامَنَتۡ فَنَفَعَهَآ إِيمَٰنُهَآ إِلَّا قَوۡمَ يُونُسَ لَمَّآ ءَامَنُواْ كَشَفۡنَا عَنۡهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡخِزۡيِ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَمَتَّعۡنَٰهُمۡ إِلَىٰ حِينࣲ‏

6:76.ar: فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلَّيۡلُ رَءَا كَوۡكَبࣰ اۖ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلۡأٓفِلِينَ
6:76.en: When the night grew dark upon him he beheld a star. He said: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: I love not things that set

6:77.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلۡقَمَرَ بَازِغࣰ ا قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّيۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ قَالَ لَئِن لَّمۡ يَهۡدِنِي رَبِّي لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
6:77.en: And when he saw the moon uprising, he exclaimed: This is my Lord. But when it set, he said: Unless my Lord guide me, I surely shall become one of the folk who are astray

6:78.ar: فَلَمَّا رَءَا ٱلشَّمۡسَ بَازِغَةࣰ قَالَ هَٰذَا رَبِّي هَٰذَآ أَكۡبَرُۖ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتۡ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ إِنِّي بَرِيٓءࣱ مِّمَّا تُشۡرِكُونَ
6:78.en: And when he saw the sun uprising, he cried: This is my Lord! This is greater! And when it set he exclaimed: O my people! Lo! I am free from all that ye associate (with Him)

21:57.ar: وَتَٱللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصۡنَٰمَكُم بَعۡدَ أَن تُوَلُّواْ مُدۡبِرِينَ
21:57.en: And, by Allah, I shall circumvent your idols after ye have gone away and turned your backs

21:58.ar: فَجَعَلَهُمۡ جُذَٰذًا إِلَّا كَبِيرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ لَعَلَّهُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ يَرۡجِعُونَ

2:260.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيۡفَ تُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ قَالَ أَوَلَمۡ تُؤۡمِنۖ قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطۡمَئِنَّ قَلۡبِيۖ قَالَ فَخُذۡ أَرۡبَعَةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلطَّيۡرِ فَصُرۡهُنَّ إِلَيۡكَ ثُمَّ ٱجۡعَلۡ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلࣲ مِّنۡهُنَّ جُزۡءࣰ ا ثُمَّ ٱدۡعُهُنَّ يَأۡتِينَكَ سَعۡيࣰ اۚ وَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
2:260.en: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise

shksM8YdDfg.speaker: adnan
shksM8YdDfg.speaker_note: 15th installment of his 'Achieving the Balance' series
shksM8YdDfg.title: Achieving the Balance: Between Understanding the Wisdom and Full Submission
shksM8YdDfg.one_line: Everything Allah creates and commands has wisdom, but faith cannot depend on explaining everything; a Muslim submits, then serves those who suffer.
shksM8YdDfg.summary: The fifteenth balance khutbah opens with the undisputed part: Allah created nothing aimlessly, the cosmos serves a purpose, and every command ends with its aim, such as taqwa or guidance. The balance is that knowing there is wisdom does not mean you will always see it. Faith built on needing an explanation for every event will eventually collapse, because the word Muslim means one who submits unconditionally. He argues that believers trust Allah because of pain, not despite it: at the Trench the believers saw ten thousand enemies and said this is what Allah promised, and the Quran states that trials are promised to every claimant of faith. Those who understand do not ask why disasters happen; they get up and relieve suffering. No one knows why the people of Yunus were spared and Pharaoh was not. Ibrahim, the most questioning prophet, who reasoned about idols and stars and asked to see resurrection, submitted when told to sacrifice his son without any reason given. Applying this to the recent earthquake and to a toddler dying of cancer, he says servants provide the service and do not question the Master, and he condemns those who explain catastrophes as punishment for victims' sins as arrogant and harmful.

outline.heading: Opening
Nothing was created for play
outline.gist: Undisputed ground: everything Allah created has a purpose and every command has a goal. Did you think We created you aimlessly and that you would not return to Us?

outline.heading: Creation subjected to serve you
outline.gist: Rain, ships, rivers, sun, moon, night and day are placed at your disposal; the sun and moon let you count your years; the oaths by winds and clouds show that everything has a role.

outline.heading: Every command ends with its aim
outline.gist: Verses on prayer, fasting and zakah close with their goal: taqwa, guidance, the straight path. Beyond the truth there is only error, and he recites further verses on purposeful creation.

outline.heading: Wisdom you will not always see
outline.gist: Knowing there is wisdom behind everything does not mean you will know it. Faith built on needing an explanation for every event will, with certainty, be lost.

outline.heading: What 'Muslim' means
outline.gist: A Muslim is one who accepts unconditionally what Allah says and does, including what cannot be explained.

outline.heading: Because of the pain, not despite it
outline.gist: Atheists reject God because of suffering and some Muslims believe despite it; he argues believers trust Allah because of it, since He foretold it.

outline.heading: The Trench: this is what Allah promised
outline.gist: After ten days of digging, the believers saw ten thousand Confederates and said this is what Allah promised, while the doubters called the promise a lie; the sight only strengthened their faith.

outline.heading: Trials are promised to every claimant of faith
outline.gist: We do not question Allah; we respond. People will not be left to say 'we believe' without being tested, so Allah makes evident who is truthful and who strives and perseveres.

outline.heading: Shaken until they asked when help would come
outline.gist: Earlier believers were shaken to their core until the Prophet and those with him asked when Allah's help would come; it is near. The question is what you do when trials come.

outline.heading: We have exaggerated our power to explain
outline.gist: Having worked out the reasons for some commands, people think everything must be explainable and lose faith when something is not. A Muslim accepts what Allah decreed either way.

outline.heading: Put your head down and do the job
outline.gist: When catastrophe strikes, the ignorant ask why and who; those who understand go and relieve the suffering. Questioning Allah is beyond your and my payroll.

outline.heading: Why were the people of Yunus spared?
outline.gist: Yunus's people were warned of punishment and then spared, while Pharaoh was not. We do not know why, never will, and it is not our business.

outline.heading: Ibrahim told to sacrifice his son
outline.gist: He is not preaching blind faith and has been criticized for saying the opposite, but no one can give a reason for slaughtering an only son; the Quran praises the moment they both submitted.

outline.heading: Ibrahim the questioner: idols and stars
outline.gist: Ibrahim is the most intellectual prophet in the Quran: he broke the idols to expose them and reasoned through the star, moon and sun.

outline.heading: Shown the birds, yet submitting without a reason
outline.gist: He asked to see how Allah revives the dead and was shown the birds on the mountains, yet when no reason for the sacrifice could be found he submitted, which is what Muslim means.

outline.heading: A child's cancer: servants serve, not question
outline.gist: Some things, like a toddler dying of cancer, have no explanation available to us. His job is to submit, comfort and help the family; servants provide the service and do not question the Master, and one day Allah will explain.

outline.heading: The earthquake and the arrogance of blaming victims
outline.gist: Forcing an explanation on the earthquake leads people to say the victims were punished for their sins. That is arrogance and speaking without knowledge, and it drives people from faith; we ask for mercy, help and thank Allah we were spared.

outline.heading: Outro

36:47.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمۡ أَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَنُطۡعِمُ مَن لَّوۡ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ أَطۡعَمَهُۥٓ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
36:47.en: And when it is said unto them: Spend of that wherewith Allah hath provided you, those who disbelieve say unto those who believe: Shall we feed those whom Allah, if He willed, would feed? Ye are in naught else than error manifest

36:48.ar: وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَىٰ هَٰذَا ٱلۡوَعۡدُ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
36:48.en: And they say: When will this promise be fulfilled, if ye are truthful

36:49.ar: مَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ تَأۡخُذُهُمۡ وَهُمۡ يَخِصِّمُونَ
36:49.en: They await but one Shout, which will surprise them while they are disputing

36:50.ar: فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ تَوۡصِيَةࣰ وَلَآ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُونَ
36:50.en: Then they cannot make bequest, nor can they return to their own folk

36:51.ar: وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ فَإِذَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمۡ يَنسِلُونَ
36:51.en: And the trumpet is blown and lo! from the graves they hie unto their Lord

36:52.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰوَيۡلَنَا مَنۢ بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرۡقَدِنَاۜۗ هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلۡمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:52.en: Crying: Woe upon us! Who hath raised us from our place of sleep? This is that which the Beneficent did promise, and the messengers spoke truth

36:53.ar: إِن كَانَتۡ إِلَّا صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَإِذَا هُمۡ جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:53.en: It is but one Shout, and behold them brought together before Us

36:54.ar: فَٱلۡيَوۡمَ لَا تُظۡلَمُ نَفۡسࣱ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
36:54.en: This day no soul is wronged in aught; nor are ye requited aught save what ye used to do

5:18.ar: وَقَالَتِ ٱلۡيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ نَحۡنُ أَبۡنَٰٓؤُاْ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّٰٓؤُهُۥۚ قُلۡ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُمۖ بَلۡ أَنتُم بَشَرࣱ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقَۚ يَغۡفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلۡكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَاۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
5:18.en: The Jews and Christians say: We are sons of Allah and His loved ones. Say: Why then doth He chastise you for your sins? Nay, ye are but mortals of His creating. He forgiveth whom He will, and chastiseth whom He will. Allah's is the Sovereignty of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, and unto Him is the journeying

28:56.ar: إِنَّكَ لَا تَهۡدِي مَنۡ أَحۡبَبۡتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
28:56.en: Lo! thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest, but Allah guideth whom He will. And He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

43:32.ar: أَهُمۡ يَقۡسِمُونَ رَحۡمَتَ رَبِّكَۚ نَحۡنُ قَسَمۡنَا بَيۡنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَرَفَعۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ فَوۡقَ بَعۡضࣲ دَرَجَٰتࣲ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعۡضُهُم بَعۡضࣰ ا سُخۡرِيࣰّ اۗ وَرَحۡمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ
43:32.en: Is it they who apportion thy Lord's mercy? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of the world, and raised some of them above others in rank that some of them may take labour from others; and the mercy of thy Lord is better than (the wealth) that they amass

4:40.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَظۡلِمُ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲۖ وَإِن تَكُ حَسَنَةࣰ يُضَٰعِفۡهَا وَيُؤۡتِ مِن لَّدُنۡهُ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
4:40.en: Lo! Allah wrongeth not even of the weight of an ant; and if there is a good deed, He will double it and will give (the doer) from His presence an immense reward

31:16.ar: يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنَّهَآ إِن تَكُ مِثۡقَالَ حَبَّةࣲ مِّنۡ خَرۡدَلࣲ فَتَكُن فِي صَخۡرَةٍ أَوۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ أَوۡ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَأۡتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
31:16.en: O my dear son! Lo! though it be but the weight of a grain of mustard-seed, and though it be in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Lo! Allah is Subtile, Aware

99:7.ar: فَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيۡرࣰ ا يَرَهُۥ
99:7.en: And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then

99:8.ar: وَمَن يَعۡمَلۡ مِثۡقَالَ ذَرَّةࣲ شَرࣰّ ا يَرَهُۥ
99:8.en: And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then

89:15.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ
89:15.en: As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me

89:16.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
89:16.en: But whenever He trieth him by straitening his means of life, he saith: My Lord despiseth me

28:76.ar: ۞إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوۡمِ مُوسَىٰ فَبَغَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۖ وَءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلۡكُنُوزِ مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓأُ بِٱلۡعُصۡبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُوَّةِ إِذۡ قَالَ لَهُۥ قَوۡمُهُۥ لَا تَفۡرَحۡۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡفَرِحِينَ
28:76.en: Now Korah was of Moses' folk, but he oppressed them; and We gave him so much treasure that the stores thereof would verily have been a burden for a troop of mighty men. When his own folk said unto him: Exult not; lo! Allah loveth not the exultant

28:77.ar: وَٱبۡتَغِ فِيمَآ ءَاتَىٰكَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۖ وَلَا تَنسَ نَصِيبَكَ مِنَ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ وَأَحۡسِن كَمَآ أَحۡسَنَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيۡكَۖ وَلَا تَبۡغِ ٱلۡفَسَادَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُفۡسِدِينَ
28:77.en: But seek the abode of the Hereafter in that which Allah hath given thee and neglect not thy portion of the world, and be thou kind even as Allah hath been kind to thee, and seek not corruption in the earth; lo! Allah loveth not corrupters

28:78.ar: قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلۡمٍ عِندِيٓۚ أَوَلَمۡ يَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدۡ أَهۡلَكَ مِن قَبۡلِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡقُرُونِ مَنۡ هُوَ أَشَدُّ مِنۡهُ قُوَّةࣰ وَأَكۡثَرُ جَمۡعࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُسۡـَٔلُ عَن ذُنُوبِهِمُ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
28:78.en: He said: I have been given it only on account of knowledge I possess. Knew he not that Allah had destroyed already of the generations before him men who were mightier than him in strength and greater in respect of following? The guilty are not questioned of their sins

28:79.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
28:79.en: Then went he forth before his people in his pomp. Those who were desirous of the life of the world said: Ah, would that we had the like of what hath been given unto Korah! Lo! he is lord of rare good fortune

28:80.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ وَيۡلَكُمۡ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ
28:80.en: But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe unto you! The reward of Allah for him who believeth and doeth right is better, and only the steadfast will obtain it

28:81.ar: فَخَسَفۡنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةࣲ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنتَصِرِينَ
28:81.en: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling-place. Then he had no host to help him against Allah, nor was he of those who can save themselves

28:82.ar: وَأَصۡبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوۡاْ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيۡكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَاۖ وَيۡكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
28:82.en: And morning found those who had coveted his place but yesterday crying: Ah, welladay! Allah enlargeth the provision for whom He will of His slaves and straiteneth it (for whom He will). If Allah had not been gracious unto us He would have caused it to swallow us (also). Ah, welladay! the disbelievers never prosper

4:49.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُمۚ بَلِ ٱللَّهُ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَآءُ وَلَا يُظۡلَمُونَ فَتِيلًا
4:49.en: Hast thou not seen those who praise themselves for purity? Nay, Allah purifieth whom He will, and they will not be wronged even the hair upon a date-stone

4:9.ar: وَلۡيَخۡشَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَوۡ تَرَكُواْ مِنۡ خَلۡفِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّةࣰ ضِعَٰفًا خَافُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ فَلۡيَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَلۡيَقُولُواْ قَوۡلࣰ ا سَدِيدًا
4:9.en: And let those fear (in their behaviour toward orphans) who if they left behind them weak offspring would be afraid for them. So let them mind their duty to Allah, and speak justly

54:17.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:17.en: And in truth We have made the Qur'an easy to remember; but is there any that remembereth

7:187.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلسَّاعَةِ أَيَّانَ مُرۡسَىٰهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ رَبِّيۖ لَا يُجَلِّيهَا لِوَقۡتِهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ ثَقُلَتۡ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ لَا تَأۡتِيكُمۡ إِلَّا بَغۡتَةࣰۗ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ كَأَنَّكَ حَفِيٌّ عَنۡهَاۖ قُلۡ إِنَّمَا عِلۡمُهَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
7:187.en: They ask thee of the (destined) Hour, when will it come to port. Say: Knowledge thereof is with my Lord only. He alone will manifest it at its proper time. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It cometh not to you save unawares. They question thee as if thou couldst be well informed thereof. Say: Knowledge thereof is with Allah only, but most of mankind know not

79:42.en: They ask thee of the Hour: when will it come to port

79:43.en: Why (ask they)? What hast thou to tell thereof

79:44.en: Unto thy Lord belongeth (knowledge of) the term thereof

79:45.en: Thou art but a warner unto him who feareth it

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

70:43.ar: يَوۡمَ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ سِرَاعࣰ ا كَأَنَّهُمۡ إِلَىٰ نُصُبࣲ يُوفِضُونَ
70:43.en: The day when they come forth from the graves in haste, as racing to a goal

78:40.ar: إِنَّآ أَنذَرۡنَٰكُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا قَرِيبࣰ ا يَوۡمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلۡمَرۡءُ مَا قَدَّمَتۡ يَدَاهُ وَيَقُولُ ٱلۡكَافِرُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي كُنتُ تُرَٰبَۢا
78:40.en: Lo! We warn you of a doom at hand, a day whereon a man will look on that which his own hands have sent before, and the disbeliever will cry: "Would that I were dust

36:15.ar: قَالُواْ مَآ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا بَشَرࣱ مِّثۡلُنَا وَمَآ أَنزَلَ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنُ مِن شَيۡءٍ إِنۡ أَنتُمۡ إِلَّا تَكۡذِبُونَ
36:15.en: They said: Ye are but mortals like unto us. The Beneficent hath naught revealed. Ye do but lie

36:16.ar: قَالُواْ رَبُّنَا يَعۡلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيۡكُمۡ لَمُرۡسَلُونَ
36:16.en: They answered: Our Lord knoweth that we are indeed sent unto you

36:32.ar: وَإِن كُلࣱّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعࣱ لَّدَيۡنَا مُحۡضَرُونَ
36:32.en: But all, without exception, will be brought before Us

jfCuAIj8veY.speaker_note: Friday Arabic tafsir series on Surah Ya-Sin, continuing from the previous week
jfCuAIj8veY.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surah Ya-Sin (36:47-54)
jfCuAIj8veY.one_line: Why 'shall we feed whom Allah could feed' is a diseased worldview, and the sudden Hour, the two blasts and the resurrection in Ya-Sin.
jfCuAIj8veY.summary: He returns to the verse in which disbelievers refuse to spend, asking why they should feed someone Allah could feed. He calls this a diseased understanding that spreads to everything: why call people to guidance if Allah could guide them? Allah deliberately made people unequal in wealth, health and guidance so they serve and need one another; full justice is reserved for the Day of Judgment. Wealth is a test, not a sign of favour, and those who claim to be Allah's beloved repeat an error the Quran warns Muslims against. The Prophet kept nothing and died with his armour pawned, and everything good grows by being spent. Moving to the next verses, he condemns asking when the Hour will come and the obsession with its signs; the task is to obey, call and spend until the last breath, as in the hadith of planting a sapling. The Hour strikes mid-conversation, leaving no time for a bequest. He explains the two blasts, the word for graves that always comes with rushing to Allah, and the two rules of the reckoning: no injustice, yet we survive only by His grace. A soul cannot live unless attached to the Hereafter.

outline.heading: Why he paused on the spending verse
outline.gist: The verse marks a real error that separates believers from others in how they understand life and Allah's purpose.

outline.heading: Real life is obeying and calling to Allah
outline.gist: Obeying without seeing a role in drawing people to Allah is a clear gap in understanding obedience.

outline.heading: Recap: the believer of Ya-Sin and the three signs
outline.gist: He called his people despite every excuse and likely death; he died, yet his mention lives on in the Quran.

outline.heading: 'Shall we feed whom Allah could feed?'
outline.gist: The refusal says: if Allah wanted this done He would do it, so why ask me; he calls it a diseased understanding.

outline.heading: The same logic applied to guidance
outline.gist: Why call anyone if Allah could guide them? Provision here includes knowledge and guidance, and the same excuse is used for all of it.

outline.heading: Where Muslim and non-Muslim understanding part
outline.gist: Grasping this verse correctly is what distinguishes the Muslim's view of the world.

outline.heading: Disparity is by design so people need each other
outline.gist: Allah enriches some and impoverishes others, heals some and tests others, guides some so they call the rest.

outline.heading: Full justice is apportioned on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: Worldly shares are unequal by design; on the Day not an atom's weight of good or evil is lost.

outline.heading: Serve others now; your hour of need will come
outline.gist: Everyone eventually needs others; serving with what you have is a plea that Allah will send help when you need it.

outline.heading: Wealth and poverty are both tests
outline.gist: Taking abundance as proof of Allah's love and hardship as proof of His contempt are both wrong.

outline.heading: Qarun: 'I was given it for knowledge I have'
outline.gist: He credited his own effort, refused to share with the 'lazy', and was swallowed by the earth, teaching onlookers the truth.

outline.heading: Given in order to give
outline.gist: Ya-Sin says obedience and love of the religion revive the soul, which requires knowing that you are given so you pass it on.

outline.heading: Nothing personal: what you are given is a test
outline.gist: No one is favoured; guidance, wealth or poverty are handed to you and you will be asked what you did with them.

outline.heading: Not Allah's pampered children
outline.gist: The verse about those who called themselves Allah's beloved is there so Muslims avoid the same claim; only Allah purifies whom He wills.

outline.heading: Impudence toward the Giver
outline.gist: He who gave can take away; many proud people ended up begging, so fear for yourself and your children.

outline.heading: The Prophet kept nothing
outline.gist: He spent everything that came to him and died with his armour pawned to a Jewish man, leaving no worldly inheritance.

outline.heading: Everything good grows by being spent
outline.gist: He corrects the saying that wealth shrinks with spending: charity does not decrease wealth, and a spender stops fearing numbers.

outline.heading: 'Do not count, or Allah will count against you'
outline.gist: The Prophet told a wife counting her money to give without tallying.

outline.heading: Your legal right is a trust before Allah
outline.gist: No one may take your property by law, but between you and Allah whatever you have, from time to status, is lent to be used for Him and for those without.

outline.heading: 'If we give, the poor will compete with us'
outline.gist: Keeping others weak so one's family stays strong is the same dead-souled logic of the verse.

outline.heading: Recitation: 'When is this promise?'
outline.gist: He recites the question and the answer that a single blast awaits them.

outline.heading: Why 'yakhissimun': merging close letters
outline.gist: Arabs merge letters of close articulation for ease, as in muddakir; here the ta merges into the sad.

outline.heading: Recitation: the trumpet and the rising
outline.gist: He recites the verses on the trumpet and the dead rising from their graves.

outline.heading: The light pause after 'our sleeping place'
outline.gist: In Hafs by way of ash-Shatibiyyah one pauses briefly without breath so the listener does not join 'this' to the question.

outline.heading: Recitation: one blast, all brought before Us
outline.gist: He recites the closing verses of the passage.

outline.heading: The Day of Judgment in every surah
outline.gist: Every long surah mentions it, because life and behaviour make no sense without it.

outline.heading: Muslims disconnected from accountability
outline.gist: After long colonisation, some non-Muslims live as if they will meet God while practising Muslims wrong others and shop for permissive fatwas.

outline.heading: The Prophet invites retaliation before his death
outline.gist: He asked anyone whose wealth, honour or back he had harmed to take it back, so he could meet Allah owing nothing to people.

outline.heading: 'When' is not your question
outline.gist: The Prophet answered the question of when with 'what have you prepared'; knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah alone.

outline.heading: It comes suddenly, mid-argument
outline.gist: Unlike films with warning music, the blast takes them while they are disputing and chatting.

outline.heading: Hadith: the Hour strikes mid-task
outline.gist: A man repairing his basin, two men selling a garment, a man raising a morsel to his mouth: none finishes.

outline.heading: Stop obsessing over the signs of the Hour
outline.gist: The Quran mentions major signs only a few times; using them to calculate dates is foolish and distracts from one's duty.

outline.heading: What the minor signs are for
outline.gist: They should push us away from sin and toward teaching people, not breed despair and passive waiting with popcorn.

outline.heading: Plant the sapling even as the Hour comes
outline.gist: Keep working at obedience and calling people until the last breath; the timing is not your task.

outline.heading: No time for a bequest or return to family
outline.gist: There is no deathbed farewell; the one Allah warns before death is fortunate.

outline.heading: Are you ready if you die today?
outline.gist: No one is promised a warning or a safe return home, so who here is truly ready?

outline.heading: Hadith: 'All of it remains except its shoulder'

outline.heading: Why the Hour follows the spending verse

rtA8Kn0h7p0.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Waqi'ah, Part 5 (56:75-96)
rtA8Kn0h7p0.one_line: The oath by the positions of the stars, the nobility of the Quran, the soul at the throat, and the three final destinations.
rtA8Kn0h7p0.summary: He closes Al-Waqi'ah by recalling how the cluster of surahs from Qaf onward offers choices, ending with the three groups on the Day of Judgment, where worldly labels like degrees and nationality vanish. A one-in-three chance of ruin is not a gamble worth taking, and he describes the private reckoning, counting life as roughly four thousand weeks, and the verdict as the climax every life story should build toward. He then explains Allah's emphatic oath by the positions of the stars, linking nujum to the Quran revealed in instalments, the vastness of the cosmos and our smallness, and the three senses of karim: noble, rare and endlessly generous. The Quran is preserved and sent by the Lord of all that is not God. He asks why anyone would bargain away parts of this way of life or make denial their thanks for it, then describes the soul at the throat with Allah nearer than the family, citing the long hadith on death. He urges aiming to be among those brought near, removing the idea of deserving, and explains the levels of certainty. Finally he asks students to read the Quran as if it were revealed to them personally and to respond to Allah's communication.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: the cluster of surahs as a series of choices
outline.gist: From Qaf onward each surah offers a choice: righteousness, purpose, guidance, certainty of knowledge, gratitude.

outline.heading: Three groups, and worldly labels dissolve
outline.gist: On the Day of Judgment degrees, professions and nationalities mean nothing; only how you lived decides your group.

outline.heading: A one-in-three risk is not worth gambling
outline.gist: Drawing on giving survival odds to patients, he argues no chance of ending in the wrong group is acceptable.

outline.heading: The private reckoning with your book
outline.gist: Narrations describe being brought before Allah, screened from others, and asked to read through your record.

outline.heading: A life is about four thousand weeks
outline.gist: A lifetime is about a thousand months; each week is like one page you must explain.

outline.heading: Asked also about what you did not do
outline.gist: You will be asked about the person Allah sent your way whom you brushed off because you were busy.

outline.heading: The verdict as the climax of your story
outline.gist: Hearing that you made it makes every hardship worthwhile; a life indifferent to that moment is like a film whose hero ignores the plot.

outline.heading: Those promised Paradise still feared
outline.gist: Companions who heard directly that they were in Jannah never lowered their guard; aim high.

outline.heading: Recitation note: prolongation counts in Hafs
outline.gist: Most prolongations are four counts in Hafs; a few places take six, which he points out.

outline.heading: An oath that begins 'No, I swear'
outline.gist: The la before the oath emphasises rather than negates: Allah does not need to swear but does so to stress what follows.

outline.heading: Nujum: the stars and the Quran revealed in instalments
outline.gist: The word evokes both stars in the sky and the Quran sent down in parts; the answer to the oath is that this is a noble Quran.

outline.heading: Karim: noble, rare and endlessly generous
outline.gist: The Quran is of high status, has nothing like it, and keeps giving the more you read it.

outline.heading: A mighty oath, if you only knew
outline.gist: Light years and galaxies are beyond comprehension; we are small and simple, yet were given this book.

outline.heading: In a protected record, touched only by the purified
outline.gist: The Quran is kept with Allah and handled only by the angels who carry it to the prophets.

outline.heading: We used to look up at the sky
outline.gist: Before phones people stared upward; most named stars carry Arabic names; the fiqh of touching the mushaf is not the point here.

outline.heading: Sent down by the Lord of all worlds
outline.gist: Al-'alamin is everything other than Allah, so unlike earlier scriptures sent to particular peoples, the Quran addresses all creation.

outline.heading: What else do you need to hear?
outline.gist: After such an oath, he asks what is still missing before one turns one's life around.

outline.heading: Hadith as a way of life
outline.gist: The word means a way of life and conduct, which is why the Prophet's sayings, actions and approvals are all called hadith.

outline.heading: Selling out on parts of the book
outline.gist: Mudhinun are those who compromise principles for gain; believers cannot bargain pieces of the deen away as people with nothing to lose do.

outline.heading: Making denial your thanks for provision
outline.gist: The Quran is the most elite provision; repaying it with denial and neglect is the ingratitude the verse condemns.

outline.heading: The soul at the throat, and We are nearer
outline.gist: As the family watches the dying, Allah and the angels of death are closer to the person than they are.

outline.heading: The long hadith of death and the grave
outline.gist: The Prophet sat by a grave, told them to seek refuge from its punishment, and described angels of light coming for the believer's soul.

outline.heading: If you are not accountable, hold the soul back
outline.gist: Madinin means held to account; no technology or ICU can keep the soul in, since every organ carries an expiry date.

outline.heading: If he is among those brought near
outline.gist: Those brought near are the forerunners from the start of the surah; aim to be among them.

outline.heading: Remove 'deserve' from your vocabulary
outline.gist: No one deserves anything from Allah, so feeling unworthy is no reason not to aim high.

outline.heading: Rest, fragrance and a garden of bliss
outline.gist: Rawh is a breath of relief that removes anxiety and emptiness; the highest reward is inner peace before anything physical.

outline.heading: Peace from the people of the right
outline.gist: They send their greetings of peace because they are doing well; there is no need to worry about them.

outline.heading: The deniers and the astray
outline.gist: Whether one rejects truth knowingly or drifts in indifference, the end is boiling water and burning fire.

outline.heading: The truth of certainty
outline.gist: He distinguishes certainty from knowledge, from seeing and from experience; on the Day you will experience it, so choose now which of the three you want.

outline.heading: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great
outline.gist: The second time the command appears; glorify Allah and look inward for answers rather than blaming Him.

outline.heading: The closing passage drawn together
outline.gist: He retells the whole sequence from the oath to the three destinations in one sweep.

outline.heading: Interlude
Muslims missing the beauty of their book
outline.gist: It pains him that many Muslims only know the Quran from school or prayer and miss its depth and philosophy.

outline.heading: Three dimensions of the Quran
outline.gist: When a surah was revealed, where it sits in the mushaf, and what it does to you; only the third he cannot do for you.

outline.heading: Read it as if revealed to you
outline.gist: His teacher had students read as if they were the Prophet receiving it, then as if it were sent to them personally to practise and spread.

outline.heading: Allah's message awaits your response
outline.gist: Communication is two-way; Allah's side is done, and what remains is how you live by, defend and spread it.

outline.heading: Outro
Read the surah yourself first
outline.gist: Come to your own understanding before each lesson and compare, to build the skill of personal reflection.

e0FT0-DBM0A.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Waqi'ah, Part 4 (56:57-74)
e0FT0-DBM0A.one_line: Four questions in Al-Waqi'ah (procreation, crops, rain, fire) that strip away human arrogance and build full conviction that Allah created us.
e0FT0-DBM0A.summary: He presents this page of Al-Waqi'ah as the surah's philosophical case for choosing to be among the foremost or the people of the right. It opens with the challenge that Allah created us, so why do we not believe. He argues that when Muslims fail to practise, the root is often not weak will but a hidden doubt in conviction, and that untreated doubt spreads like a cancer. The passage then asks four questions about things everyone takes for granted. Who turns the fluid into a human being? Who makes the seed grow? Who sends fresh water from the clouds instead of salt? Who made the tree that gives fire? In each case our contribution is only to bring things together and hope. He uses embryology, fertility treatment, farming, the water cycle and the difficulty of even defining fire to show that science explains how a process works, never who set it in motion, and that understanding a process should deepen awe rather than replace God. Because religion rests on such simple shared facts, everyone can be held accountable. He closes with the command to exalt the name of the Lord and urges the audience to reach certainty, since certainty changes habits, behaviour and how one sees the world.

outline.heading: Al-Waqi'ah as a surah of choices
outline.gist: The surah keeps offering the listener a choice of who to be: guided or aimless, grateful or ungrateful.

outline.heading: A page that argues why you should choose well
outline.gist: Before the closing comparison, this page breaks off to give philosophical reasons to join the first two groups.

outline.heading: We created you, so why do you not believe?
outline.gist: The anchor verse: the proper response to being created is belief, and refusing it points to something unresolved inside.

outline.heading: Weak practice hides a problem of conviction
outline.gist: Beneath laziness and desire lies doubt; Makkan surahs focus on belief because once certainty is built, practice follows and no one can stop you.

outline.heading: Untreated doubt grows like cancer
outline.gist: Doubt never sits quietly; it spreads and eats the good around it unless dealt with.

outline.heading: Questions that force an answer
outline.gist: Like the repeated question in Ar-Rahman, these verses pose four questions about four basic things everyone agrees on.

outline.heading: The fluid you emit: do you create it?
outline.gist: Our role in procreation is only bringing two fluids together; the differentiation of cells into a human being is entirely beyond us.

outline.heading: Science explains how, not who
outline.gist: Science gives a more detailed description, not an answer to origin; confusing science with philosophy is a modern fallacy.

outline.heading: If the process simply stopped
outline.gist: If gametes stopped combining, no one could negotiate with them and humanity would vanish in a generation.

outline.heading: We decreed death and none can outrun Us
outline.gist: Every human carries an expiry date; Allah alone decrees the moment of death.

outline.heading: Replacing you and re-forming you in what you do not know
outline.gist: Our consciousness could have been channelled into any other form; being a functioning human is a gift we underrate.

outline.heading: Fertility clinics only make a better introduction
outline.gist: Even assisted reproduction just brings egg and sperm together; the intricate dance of DNA happens on its own.

outline.heading: You know the first creation, so why deny the second?
outline.gist: The same power that brought us out the first time can bring us out again; tadhakkur means reflecting on this.

outline.heading: Human arrogance after a little knowledge
outline.gist: Humans understand one equation and then deny God, because knowledge feels powerful; imagine the One who knows all.

outline.heading: The crops you sow: do you make them grow?
outline.gist: Zar' is making a seed become a plant that bears food; we supply soil, water and light, but a dead seed coming to life is not our doing.

outline.heading: Skilled farming versus the source of life
outline.gist: Farming expertise clutters the question with irrelevant detail; where the life in the plant comes from is untouched by it.

outline.heading: Turned to debris: we are ruined, we are deprived
outline.gist: If seeds stopped growing, people would wander speaking aimlessly in the language of doom, deprived of all food.

outline.heading: The water you drink: who sends it from the clouds?
outline.gist: All earth's water was salty; fresh reservoirs come from billions of years of the sun evaporating sea water at just the right distance.

outline.heading: Had We willed, We would have made it salty
outline.gist: Imagine acid or salt rain; we expect children, harvests and rain as givens and owe gratitude because we control none of it.

outline.heading: Ten years without rain
outline.gist: A region his family knew for deep snow turned near-desert after a decade of drought; people in water-rich places complain about rain because they have not seen its absence.

outline.heading: The fire you kindle and the tree that feeds it
outline.gist: We only create friction; Allah made the wood that burns, and human history changed once fire was harnessed.

outline.heading: A reminder and provision for travellers, and a thing we cannot define
outline.gist: Fire recalls punishment and serves those on life's journey; scientists still do not agree on what fire actually is.

outline.heading: Understanding the process should increase awe
outline.gist: Like a child who appreciates parents only once raising children, knowing how something works should deepen appreciation of who made it.

outline.heading: Simple basics everyone can be held to
outline.gist: Recap of the four questions; religion rests on facts all share equally, which is why everyone can be held accountable.

outline.heading: Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great
outline.gist: The closing command follows from the four questions: glorify the One who made it so.

rbiOm_SFpzA.title: The Battle of Khaybar
rbiOm_SFpzA.one_line: The march on Khaybar: doing your best with what you have, fairness, the group over the individual, inner conviction, art for morale, and the banner given to Ali.
rbiOm_SFpzA.summary: The sheikh explains why the Prophet marched on Khaybar in year seven: it had become the centre of plotting against Madinah and refused every treaty, so he aimed to besiege its fortresses and force terms with little bloodshed. With 1400 people against ten thousand behind walls never breached, he went anyway, and the sheikh draws a principle: give everything you have, plan thoroughly, then sleep well and leave the outcome to Allah. Stories along the way illustrate his teaching. The Prophet made a companion repay a creditor even if it cost him a fighter, and an elderly woman funded that companion's journey. A man who rode ahead against orders was sent to the rear and ignored for a day, which leads to a strong warning against isolating yourself from the community to criticise it from outside. He describes the intelligence work that turned Ghatafan back, the takbir of the night whose conviction unsettled the defenders, and how distraction keeps people from building that inner strength. A starving companion who nearly ate alone is used to separate healthy individuality from selfishness. He defends art and poetry as vital to a community's morale, and ends with the Prophet's promise of the banner to one who loves Allah and His Messenger, given to Ali.

outline.heading: Opening
Why Khaybar: the remaining centre of conspiracy
outline.gist: Hudaybiyyah calmed most of Arabia, but Khaybar ignored Quraysh's lead, refused treaties and kept rallying tribes against Madinah.

outline.heading: The plan: besiege fortresses never conquered
outline.gist: A war-weary Madinah needed the threat neutralised; the Prophet chose to besiege eight huge castles 150 km away with 1400 people to force a treaty.

outline.heading: Use everything you have, then do not worry
outline.gist: Numbers never stopped the Prophet as long as he exhausted his means; if you give your best, sleep well and leave anxiety behind.

outline.heading: A snapshot of year seven: how did he cope?
outline.gist: The load he carried was overwhelming, yet he stayed steady and stood three or four hours each night in prayer.

outline.heading: Madinah's doubters: going anyway
outline.gist: Many expected the army never to return; he went because it was right, with what he had, leaving the decree to Allah.

outline.heading: Abdullah ibn Abi Hadrad and the impatient creditor
outline.gist: A creditor demands early repayment fearing the man will die at Khaybar; the Prophet tells him to pay, leaving him unable to equip himself until an elderly woman gives him something to sell.

outline.heading: No one marches without provisions
outline.gist: The Prophet barred people from joining without enough food and mounts so they would not burden others.

outline.heading: Lesson: the Prophet's fairness even at a cost
outline.gist: He sided with the creditor's right though it cost him a fighter at a critical moment.

outline.heading: Lesson: a poor but spiritually rich community
outline.gist: An old woman gave something personal to a stranger so he could go; they had little money but great spiritual wealth.

outline.heading: What goes around comes around; goodness is tested
outline.gist: The creditor later lost his orchard and needed a loan; whatever you put into the world returns, and obstacles test whether your goodness is sincere.

outline.heading: The dua for entering a new land
outline.gist: He teaches the Prophet's supplication asking for the good of a place and its people and refuge from their evil, showing he came seeking good, not blood.

outline.heading: A campaign of minimal bloodshed
outline.gist: Only about 96 people died in the whole campaign because the aim was a treaty, not war.

outline.heading: The man who rode ahead of the army
outline.gist: Told to keep together in unknown territory, one man rode far ahead on a fast camel; he was sent to the rear and no one spoke to him for a day.

outline.heading: Jama'ah over excessive individualism
outline.gist: Islam teaches living as one organism; individuality matters in your standing with Allah, but your work here is measured by what you add to the ummah.

outline.heading: Stay with the group even when you have more
outline.gist: Having a better camel is no reason to leave your brother behind; focus on contributing rather than getting ahead.

outline.heading: Never isolate yourself to preach at the community
outline.gist: One of the Prophet's rare punishments; the moment you stand apart thinking you are better, you have lost your way, even if your criticisms are right.

outline.heading: Ghatafan's alliance and failed negotiations
outline.gist: Intelligence revealed Ghatafan's four thousand would attack from behind; the Prophet offered them half of Khaybar's harvest and then warned them off.

outline.heading: Rumours that sent Ghatafan home
outline.gist: Spread through secret Muslims in the tribe, word of a planned raid on their own settlements made Ghatafan retreat until the siege was complete.

outline.heading: Doing everything includes planning and intelligence
outline.gist: The Prophet never went in blind; a strong intelligence network and contingency plans were part of exhausting every resource.

outline.heading: Khalid's testimony to the Prophet's generalship
outline.gist: Khalid said only the Prophet ever outsmarted him, reading his plan at Uhud in advance.

outline.heading: Al-Hubab's advice on the camp site
outline.gist: As at Badr, al-Hubab asked whether the position was revelation or strategy and proposed moving back out of arrow range, but only after nightfall so it would not look like fear.

outline.heading: The night takbir and the power of conviction
outline.gist: Words said with deep belief unsettled the defenders; inner calm and clarity overwhelm people who have wealth and degrees but no conviction.

outline.heading: Distraction keeps people from conviction; Muslims are not violent
outline.gist: Endless entertainment takes the hours needed to build clarity; strong Muslims are not violent but do not back down from what is right or accept oppression.

outline.heading: Fifteen days of hunger: Abdullah ibn Mughaffal's find
outline.gist: The siege dragged on and food ran out; a starving companion found some food, saw the Prophet smiling at him and shared it.

outline.heading: Healthy individuality versus selfishness
outline.gist: Individualism means Allah knows and values you, not that you matter more than others; that belief is the root of arrogance and racism.

outline.heading: Raising morale with chanted poetry
outline.gist: The Prophet asked a companion with a fine voice to chant verses from the building of the masjid, with the army answering the refrain.

outline.heading: No community rises without art
outline.gist: Youth connect through art; the Prophet used poets and artistic people, and communities that lack art struggle to attract the young.

outline.heading: The Prophet's migraine and failed assaults
outline.gist: After fourteen nights a recurring headache kept the Prophet in; two senior companions led attempts on the gate without success.

outline.heading: The banner for one who loves Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: Everyone hoped to be chosen; the Prophet called for Ali, who had an eye infection, healed it and gave him the banner.

outline.heading: Outro

QhS2ayBIxcc.title: Achieving the Balance: Desire and Fear, and the High Point of Love
QhS2ayBIxcc.one_line: Muslims fly to Allah on two wings, desire for Paradise and fear of just punishment, which together should grow into love of Allah.
QhS2ayBIxcc.summary: Opening with Allah's command to tell His servants He is most forgiving and that His punishment is painful, the fourteenth balance khutbah takes the classical image of two wings: hope in Allah's reward and fear of His punishment. He starts with desire because he thinks his society needs it: nearly every long surah describes Paradise, and wanting it is an obligation. The companions lived for it: a man threw away his dates before battle, Haritha's mother was told her son was in the highest garden, and a lame companion insisted on fighting so he could walk into Paradise on his disabled leg. In the second khutbah he objects that fear of Hell has been watered down, though the Quran never mentions one without the other. He gives five points: concepts are only understood through their opposites, as entitled children show; fear is a strong short-term brake against sin; we fear not that Allah will oppress us but that He will judge us by pure justice instead of generosity; some truly deserve punishment, so make sure you are not among them; and life contains pain, so do not shield children from it. The pinnacle is love of Allah, which outlasts both and accepts whatever He wills.

outline.heading: Opening
Tell My servants: forgiving, and painful punishment
outline.gist: The khutbah rests on the verses in which Allah tells His servants that He is the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that His punishment is painful.

outline.heading: Two wings: desire and reverent fear
outline.gist: In the fourteenth balance khutbah he gives a thousand-year-old image: you fly to Allah with hope in His reward and reverent fear of His punishment; lose one wing and you fall.

outline.heading: Desire first: Paradise in nearly every surah
outline.gist: He starts with desire because this society needs it most. Every surah of a page or more describes what awaits, and he recites the promise of Paradise to those who stay the course.

outline.heading: Bliss on every level, and wanting it is a duty
outline.gist: Paradise holds pleasures for parts of the self we have not yet discovered. Wanting it is not wrong selfishness but an obligation to work toward.

outline.heading: The companion who threw away his dates
outline.gist: Told what awaits the one who stands his ground, a companion decided eating his dates was too long a wait, gave them away, fought and was martyred.

outline.heading: Haritha in the highest garden
outline.gist: A young man killed by an arrow before the battle began; his frightened mother demanded to know his fate and was told he is in the highest of the gardens.

outline.heading: The lame companion who would walk into Paradise
outline.gist: Told all his life he could not, he refused to stay home at Uhud so his disabled leg could march into Paradise. The Prophet let him go, and he ran his uneven run to defend the mountain until he fell.

outline.heading: They lived for it, and so must we
outline.gist: The companions gave everything to be among the people of Paradise; living with that desire is what every believer is required to do.

outline.heading: Interlude
Fear of punishment has been watered down
outline.gist: People avoid talk of punishment, yet the Quran never speaks of Paradise without Hell. The Prophet saw both and said that if you knew what he knew you would laugh little and weep much.

outline.heading: Point one: nothing is understood without its opposite
outline.gist: The mind defines things only by contrast: life means something only because of death, and reward only because of punishment.

outline.heading: The entitled child: reward needs its opposite
outline.gist: Parents who made sure their children never went without are frustrated that the children do not appreciate anything; they cannot, because they never knew lack. Paradise likewise needs Hell to be understood.

outline.heading: Point two: fear as a short-term brake
outline.gist: Fear is a poor long-term motive but a strong one at the moment of sin. Without consequences people eventually do anything; the thought of punishment makes you hold back from the forbidden.

outline.heading: Point three: we fear Allah's justice, not oppression
outline.gist: We fear that people will wrong us; we never fear that from Allah. We fear that He will treat us with only justice, when what we need is generosity far beyond what we deserve.

outline.heading: Two kinds of fear a child has of a father
outline.gist: A child can fear being mistreated or fear being treated fairly and not forgiven; our fear of Allah is the second kind. He recites verses from Al-Hadid on punishment.

outline.heading: Point four: some deserve punishment; do not be among them
outline.gist: Those who oppress, kill and strip others of rights beyond repair show why Hell exists. Your only concern is to make sure your choices do not place you among them.

outline.heading: The guilty would ransom everyone
outline.gist: On seeing Hell, the guilty wish to offer their children, spouses, brothers, clans and everyone on earth to escape it; whatever they saw must be terrible to provoke that.

outline.heading: Point five: life has pain; do not shield your children
outline.gist: Suffering is part of existence. Being a good Muslim means dealing with it well, so shielding children and people from pain and from the idea of punishment is unhealthy.

outline.heading: The pinnacle: love beyond desire and fear
outline.gist: Desire and fear are the starting wings; the high point is the love of Allah they generate in the heart, for the One who loved you long before you loved Him.

outline.heading: Love accepts whatever He wills
outline.gist: Once you love Him you accept whatever He gives or withholds, because what He wants for you is what you want. Love is the strongest and longest-lasting motive.

outline.heading: Outro
